brief.subject: Trucker tax dates, NOLs at death, IRS council meeting
brief.headline: Owner-Operator Tax Deadlines, Expiring Tax Attributes and an IRS Advisory Meeting
brief.dek: Eight filing dates for owner-operators before March 1, 2027, tax breaks that vanish at death, and new IRS notices in the Federal Register.
brief.lede: Owner-operators face eight tax dates before March 1, 2027, drawn from federal rules, four states and IFTA. Now is the time to map them out.

sections.heading: Owner-Operators: Eight Dates to Calendar
bullets: Eight tax dates fall before March 1, 2027, for owner-operators, per a new calendar roundup.
The dates draw on federal rules, guidance from four states and the International Fuel Tax Agreement.
IFTA deadlines sit alongside federal ones, so fuel-tax filers juggle multiple deadline sets at once.
Mapping these dates now helps avoid penalties during the busy year-end and early-filing stretch.

sections.heading: Tax Breaks That Die With the Owner
bullets: Net operating losses and passive activity losses can disappear permanently when a taxpayer dies.
Capital loss carryforwards and unused charitable contribution carryforwards face the same risk.
The step-up in basis can still deliver significant tax benefits to heirs.
Owners carrying business losses should review which attributes survive as part of succession planning.

sections.heading: Federal Register: IRS Notices
bullets: The IRS Advisory Council will hold a public meeting, per a notice published Oct. 28.
Open meetings let practitioners track issues the council raises with IRS leadership.
The IRS also issued its quarterly list of individuals who have chosen to expatriate, dated Oct. 30.
